text:
Yuki: Quick note: small cluster of gnodes in us-east1-c reporting intermittent metadata CRCs on nvme during GPU reclaim windows. Not full failures but attach latency spikes.

infra-bot: alert: region=us-east1-c nodes=gnode-701,gnode-709 metric=nvme_meta_crc rate=0.06% window=30m

Sam R: Can you share a tiny log excerpt and whether janitor or fstrim was running?

Yuki: log: "nvme0: metadata CRC mismatch, retrying read" x6 over 40m. Janitor sweep was in-progress; deep-scrub also started in the same shard earlier tonight.

Olga: Typical race: concurrent scrub + aggressive janitor deletes cause read amplification. Short fix: lower janitor concurrency to 15% in that shard and pause deep-scrub.

Raj P: Capacity hit if we avoid nodes? How many GPUs behind these gnodes?

Yuki: 3 gnodes, ~96 GPUs total. If we tag them avoid-new-attaches we lose burst capacity but core SLA pool unaffected.

Sam R: Implement throttle + avoid tag, and add a fast-fail verification step in attach path so provisioner can skip bad candidates quickly.

infra-bot: mitigation: janitor_throttle_applied avoid_new_attaches_tag added to gnode-701,gnode-709 pause_deep_scrub

Yuki: After throttle we saw CRC log frequency drop ~70% in 20m and attach tail improved in canary. I'll collect SMART dumps to s3://redwood-debug/us-east1/meta-crc/ and open lifecycle/replacement tickets for the drives showing persistent errors.

Raj P: Thanks. Add backlog items: firmware cohort for older drives, age-aware scrub windows, and attach fast-fail PR. Post a 2-bullet note to #postmortems once stable.

Olga: Agree. Small operational change avoided a bigger drain.

Yuki: Will follow up. :thumbsup:
